newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers prospectors two gold concessions.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers prospectors two gold concessions.

text.p: The Egyptian state on Thursday invited mining companies to prospect for gold in the southwest and the east of the country.

In a published announcement, the Egyptian Geological Survey and Mining Authority (EGSMA) said the concessions were in Oweinat area in southwest Egypt, which it said comprised seven localities with good potential for gold, and in the Allaqi area in the Eastern Desert.
Interested firms should send bids along with a $500 fee to EGSMA's main office in Cairo by 1400 local time (1100 GMT) on December 31, 1997, the authority said.
The announcement did not give any more details.

The Oweinat concession is near an area where Egyptian government geologists said in June they had struck gold in a range of hills on the border with Libya. The chief geologist called it a world class discovery.
The geologists said the gold was in Jabal Kamel, a rocky outcrop close to the point where the borders of Egypt, Libya and Sudan meet.
Pharaoh Gold Mines of Australia is prospecting for gold in Egypt's Eastern Desert and plans to start gold production there in the middle of this year.
